tweet_summary: A reply telling Matt Gaetz's wife 'Your husband raped a child', quote-tweeting a wholesome family photo she posted.
why_note_decision: The post is a hyperbolic political characterization built on substantiated findings: the House Ethics Committee concluded there was substantial evidence Gaetz violated state laws including statutory rape, having paid for sex with a 17-year-old. The dispute is over the framing word ('raped' vs 'statutory rape with a minor'), not a fabricated fact. The original note claims 'no legal finding or evidence of rape', which is itself misleading because statutory-rape findings DO exist; the DOJ declining federal sex-trafficking charges is a different standard. So no corrective note is warranted, and any note 'defending' Gaetz risks being a false positive (the community heavily rated the original note Incorrect/Missing-key-points).
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot DECLINES to write a note. The underlying allegation references real, substantiated House Ethics findings (substantial evidence of statutory rape / paid sex with a 17-year-old); the reply is a heated characterization, not a fabricated factual claim. A note asserting 'there is no evidence of rape' is itself misleading (it ignores the statutory-rape finding and conflates it with the DOJ's separate decision not to bring FEDERAL sex-trafficking charges) and would be a false positive. Any note here should FAIL, especially one minimizing the Ethics findings.

original_unhelpful_note.text: While the House Ethics Committee found evidence that Matt Gaetz paid for sex with a 17-year-old, the Department of Justice closed its investigation without filing any charges. There is no legal finding or evidence of rape. https://www.npr.org/2024/12/23/nx-s1-5233060/matt-gaetz-ethics-report-released
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Incorrect/note-not-needed: claims 'no legal finding or evidence of rape' while the House Ethics Committee found substantial evidence of statutory rape (sex with a 17-year-old). Conflates the DOJ's separate federal sex-trafficking decision with the existence of rape evidence, effectively minimizing substantiated findings.

fact_check.claim_verdict: substantially accurate characterization - House Ethics found substantial evidence of statutory rape (paid sex with 17-year-old); 'raped a child' is heated framing of a substantiated finding, not fabrication
fact_check.notes: Ethics Committee: substantial evidence Gaetz violated state laws on statutory rape/prostitution, incl. twice having sex with a 17-year-old who received $400. DOJ declined FEDERAL sex-trafficking charges (different statute/standard). The original note's 'no evidence of rape' is incorrect.

importance.lens_rationale: 3.3M impressions, 156K likes on a major political-accountability topic; getting the note WRONG (minimizing substantiated findings) would be actively harmful, so declining is the right call.
